# 1 Clement Chapter 47 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 47 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_047_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 47

**47:1** Take up the epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul.

**47:2** What was the first thing he wrote to you at the beginning of the gospel?

**47:3** In truth, he wrote to you with spiritual insight concerning himself and Cephas and Apollos, because even at that time you had formed factions.

**47:4** Yet that partisanship incurred less sin, for you were making yourselves partisans of apostles who had been attested by God, and of a man approved by them.

**47:5** But now consider who it is that has perverted you and diminished the honor of your renowned brotherly affection.

**47:6** It is shameful, beloved, wholly shameful and unworthy of your manner of life in Christ, that on account of one or two persons the very steadfast and ancient church of the Corinthians is reported to be in sedition against its presbyters.

**47:7** And this report has come not only to us, but also to those who are outside our number — so that blasphemies are brought upon the name of the Lord because of your foolishness, and peril is brought upon yourselves as well.

---

*LOGOS renders according to the standard Greek text of Codex Alexandrinus with attention to formal correspondence.*
